# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 30 LORNA DECIDES

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

A swift wave of a severe form of flu at the Glen and down in the fishing village made Hugh so occupied over the following two weeks that he lacked the opportunity to make the promised call on Captain Saul. Nell continued to hope despite the odds that he had given up the notion concerning Rufus Vane, and, choosing not to stir up trouble, she mentioned the matter no further. Nevertheless, it remained constantly on her mind.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0000 }

“I ponder whether revealing to him that Lorna harbors feelings for Adrian would be proper,” she mused. “He would refrain from ever letting her guess his knowledge, meaning her pride would remain unhurt, and it MIGHT persuade him to leave Rufus Vane in peace. Ought I to—ought I to? No, when all is said, I am unable to do so. A vow is inviolable, and I possess no right to expose Lorna’s confidence. Yet oh, no matter in my life has ever caused me as much distress as this does. It is ruining the spring—it is ruining all things.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0001 }

Hugh suddenly suggested one night that they travel down to visit Captain Saul. Nell assented with a heavy heart, and the two departed. Fourteen days of gentle sun had effected a wondrous change in the dreary countryside across which Hugh’s crow had traveled. Dry, brown, and warm, the hills and fields stood prepared to burst into bud and flower; the harbor was once more quivering with laughter; like a shining red ribbon lay the long harbor road; down upon the dunes, a group of boys who had gone out smelt fishing were setting fire to the dense, dry sandhill grass from the previous summer. Across the dunes, the flames surged rosily, casting their crimson banners against the black gulf past them, and lighting up the channel alongside the fishing village. Under different circumstances, this picturesque sight would have charmed Nell’s eyes; however, she took no pleasure in this stroll. Hugh was not enjoying it either. Their customary friendly companionship and Josephian harmony of preference and perspective were regrettably absent. Nell’s rejection of the entire undertaking manifested in the arrogant tilt of her head and the deliberate courtesy of her comments. Hugh’s lips were fixed in the full stubbornness of the Carrows, yet anxiety filled his eyes. Doing what he considered his duty was his intention; nevertheless, being at odds with Nell proved a steep cost. On the whole, arriving at the light brought relief to both of them—along with guilt for feeling that relief.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0002 }

Captain Saul stowed the net he had been mending and greeted them with great joy. Nell realized he appeared older in the revealing brightness of the spring evening than he ever had before. His hair was significantly more gray, and a slight tremor affected his sturdy, aging hand. Nevertheless, his gaze remained sharp and unwavering in his blue eyes, through which his resolute spirit shone with courage and fearlessness.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0003 }

As Hugh delivered his message, Captain Saul heard him out without uttering a word, completely astonished. Understanding the depth of the old man's devotion to Lorna, Nell was convinced he would take her part, even if she doubted this would alter Hugh's stance. Consequently, she was immensely taken aback when Captain Saul declared, with a deliberate and mournful yet steadfast resolve, that Lorna ought to be informed.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0004 }

“Oh, Captain Saul, I believed you would not utter such words,” she cried in dismay. “It was my expectation that you wished to avoid creating additional difficulties for her.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0005 }

A shake of his head came from Captain Saul.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0006 }

“Refusing isn't what I wish to do. Your perspective on this matter is clear to me, Mistress Carrow—because I share those exact sentiments. However, personal emotions cannot serve as our guide in life—indeed, relying on them would frequently result in disaster. A single dependable compass exists, and we are required to navigate according to its direction—namely, performing our duty. My view aligns with the doctor's. Should an opportunity exist for Rufus, informing Lorna is necessary. As I see it, no alternative interpretation exists.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0007 }

“Well,” said Nell, surrendering to hopelessness, “just wait for Miss Winifred to go after you pair of men.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0008 }

“Winifred will surely unleash a complete barrage on us,” Captain Saul agreed. “Although you female folk are delightful beings, Mistress Carrow, a small flaw in you all is a slight lack of logic. Despite your advanced schooling compared to Winifred's lack of it, the pair of you are completely identical in this regard. Whether that makes you any less desirable is something I doubt. It seems to me that logic is rather unfeeling and stern. So, I am going to make us some tea for us to enjoy while discussing agreeable topics, simply to soothe our thoughts a little.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0009 }

At the very least, her mind was pacified so much by Captain Saul’s conversation and tea that Nell refrained from causing Hugh the sharp suffering during the journey back that she had intentionally planned for him. The burning question was not mentioned by her whatsoever, yet she conversed pleasantly about different subjects, allowing Hugh to realize that his forgiveness was granted under protest.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0010 }

“Captain Saul appears extremely weak and stooped this spring. He has been aged by the winter,” Nell remarked mournfully. “I fear he will shortly depart to search for lost Margaret. The thought of it is unbearable to me.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0011 }

“When Captain Saul 'sets out to sea,' Seven Gulls is going to be a different place,” Hugh concurred.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0012 }

He walked to the residence further up the stream the next night. Until he came back, Nell roamed about in a state of gloom.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0013 }

“So, what response did Lorna give?” was her demand upon his entry.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0014 }

“Hardly anything. It seemed to me that she was quite stunned.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0015 }

“And will the operation be performed on her?”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0016 }

“Her decision will be made very soon, after she thinks it over.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0017 }

Exhausted, Hugh dropped heavily into the armchair in front of the hearth. He had a worn appearance. Disclosing the news to Lorna had proven to be a difficult task. Furthermore, remembering the fright that flashed in her eyes as she grasped his words gave him no pleasure. At present, with the decision finalized, he found himself plagued by uncertainty regarding his own judgment.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0018 }

Nell gave him a remorseful look; after that, she slid onto the rug next to him, resting her shiny red head against his arm.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0019 }

“Hugh, I have been quite awful about this whole thing. I am not going to act that way again. Kindly just refer to me as red-headed and pardon my behavior.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0020 }

Through this, Hugh grasped that no "I told you so" would ever be uttered, regardless of the outcome. Yet his comfort remained incomplete. Duty expressed in theory is a single matter, whereas duty executed in reality is entirely different, particularly when the actor faces the desolate gaze of a woman.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0021 }

A certain intuition prompted Nell to avoid Lorna throughout the subsequent three days. Upon the third night, Lorna walked down to the small home and informed Hugh of her decision; she intended to bring Rufus to Montreal so he could undergo the operation.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0022 }

Her complexion was extremely pale, and she appeared to have enveloped herself once more in her former coat of detachment. Her eyes, however, no longer retained the expression that had troubled Hugh; instead, they were chilly and luminous, and she began talking over particulars with him in a sharp, matter-of-fact manner. Arrangements required making, and numerous matters needed consideration. As soon as Lorna obtained the facts she sought, she departed for home. Nell desired to accompany her on foot for a portion of the journey.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0023 }

“It is best you do not,” Lorna replied abruptly. “The rain that fell today has soaked the earth. Good-night.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0024 }

“Is my friend gone?” Nell asked, sighing. “Should the procedure prove effective and Rufus Vane recovers his true self, Lorna is going to withdraw to a distant sanctuary within her spirit where she will remain lost to all of us forever.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0025 }

“It may be that she will abandon him,” Hugh remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0026 }

“Lorna could not possibly act in such a manner, Hugh. A powerful feeling of obligation guides her. She mentioned to me on one occasion that Grandmother West constantly instilled in her the principle that whenever she took on a duty, she was required to fulfill it without fail, regardless of the outcome. It stands as a chief principle of hers. It seems quite out of date, I imagine.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0027 }

“Do not feel resentment, Nell-girl. You are aware that you do not consider it outmoded—you are aware that you hold the exact same belief regarding the holiness of undertaken obligations yourself. And your view is correct. Evading obligations represents the bane of our contemporary existence—the hidden cause behind all the agitation and dissatisfaction that is boiling in the world.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0028 }

“Thus saith the preacher,” Nell mocked. Yet beneath her taunting tone she recognized the truth of his words; and her heart ached deeply for Lorna.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0029 }

Seven days afterwards, Miss Winifred crashed down upon the small dwelling like a snowslide. Because Hugh was out, Nell had no choice but to endure the force of the collision by herself.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0030 }

Barely taking the time to remove her hat, Miss Winifred started right away.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0031 }

“Nell, are you trying to say that the rumors I’ve been hearing are factual—that Dr. Carrow informed Lorna that Rufus can be healed, and that she intends to bring him to Montreal so he can undergo surgery?”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0032 }

“Yes, it is entirely factual, Miss Winifred,” Nell stated courageously.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0033 }

“Well, it’s a matter of heartless savagery, that is what it amounts to,” stated Miss Winifred, who was immensely disturbed. “I truly believed Dr. Carrow to be a respectable gentleman. I never imagined he was capable of committing such a deed.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0034 }

“It was Dr. Carrow’s belief that he had a responsibility to inform Lorna that Rufus might survive,” Nell stated with vigor, “and,” she went on, her allegiance to Hugh winning out, “I am of the same mind as him.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0035 }

“Oh, no, you don’t, dearie,” remarked Miss Winifred. “Nobody possessing any bowels of compassion could.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0036 }

“Captain Saul does.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0037 }

“Do not repeat that foolish old man's words to me,” Miss Winifred exclaimed. “And regardless of who shares his opinion, it matters nothing to me. Consider—CONSIDER the consequences for that unfortunate, pursued, tormented girl.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0038 }

“It IS on our minds. However, Hugh holds the view that the well-being of a patient’s spirit and physique must be placed by a physician above every other concern.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0039 }

“That is typical of a man. Yet I anticipated a finer response from you, Nell,” remarked Miss Winifred, feeling additional grief rather than anger; after which she began to assault Nell using the exact same points that Nell had employed against Hugh; and Nell bravely shielded her spouse by utilizing the arguments he had deployed to defend himself. Extended was the battle, until Miss Winifred finally brought it to a close.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0040 }

“It is a monstrous injustice,” she announced, nearly weeping. “A monstrous injustice—that is precisely what it is. My dear, unfortunate Lorna!”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0041 }

“Wouldn’t it be right to give a bit of thought to Rufus as well?” begged Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0042 }

“Rufus! Rufus Vane! HE’S cheerful enough. Present day, he is a better behaved and more respectable part of the community than he was at any point prior.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0043 }

“Indeed, he was a heavy drinker and possibly something worse. Is it your intention to free him once more so he can bellow and destroy?”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0044 }

“He could change for the better,” stated wretched Nell, under attack by enemies on the outside and a betrayer on the inside.
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0045 }

“Reform your grandmother!” Miss Winifred retorted. “Rufus Vane received the harm that resulted in his current state during a drunken brawl. His fate is DESERVED. It was inflicted upon him as a retribution. The doctor, I don’t believe, has any right to meddle with God’s visitations.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0046 }

“It remains a mystery how Rufus suffered his injuries, Miss Winifred. A tavern fight might not be the cause. He could have been ambushed and mugged instead.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0047 }

“Swine MIGHT chirp, though their lips are ill-suited for the task,” declared Miss Winifred. “At any rate, the essence of your news indicates the matter is concluded, rendering further speech futile. Since that is the case, I will remain silent. I have no intention of ruining MY teeth by chewing on rasps. Whenever an outcome is inevitable, I yield to it. However, I prefer to be utterly certain beforehand that it truly IS unavoidable. At present, I shall apply MY efforts to soothing and supporting Lorna. Besides,” Miss Winifred continued, her mood lifting with optimism, “it is possible that Rufus is beyond help.”
{: #nw-v04-c30-p0048 }
